description: Port ONIX (open-source depletion code) to supply the MSRE depletion + fission-product inventory source term. Provides the actinide + FP isotopic evolution that feeds the FP-migration chemistry. Consider folding into outram-mc-libs (which already has a depletion path) vs a dedicated crate — decide in design. Complements a CRAM (Chebyshev Rational Approximation) Bateman-solver port from OpenMC (MIT) and ENDF/B decay + fission-yield data into njoy-outram-park-fork (separate tasks). LICENSE: ONIX believed GPL — verify upstream LICENSE and confirm GPLv3-compatibility (not GPL-2-only) before porting; keep provenance header. Pure-Rust, no FFI/PETSc/MPI. Untrusted AI-assisted draft pending human V&V.

notes.content: License due-diligence (2026-08-04): ONIX = jlanversin/ONIX, MIT/X license -> GPLv3-COMPATIBLE. CLEARED to port (keep MIT provenance). Python 3. title: Port ONIX — open-source depletion / burnup (FP inventory source term)

description: v2's physics is a cp -ar port of v1's educational_ciet_loop_version_4. The maintainer has done validation work on v1's physics, so the open question is PORT EQUIVALENCE, not the physics itself. Methodology: run v1 (tuas example) and v2 (DT engine bin) from identical initial state with identical control inputs and a fixed timestep, dump CIETState/CietState each step to CSV, and compare. Pass criterion: temperatures agree to solver round-off (suggest 1e-9 degC) over >=2000 s of simulated time. Until this runs, v2 must NOT be described as validated -- only as a faithful port of validated physics.
title: V&V: verify CIET v2 physics port reproduces v1 bit-for-bit
